## Decisions
- `Homography`/`FrameMotion` moved from `Sprocket.Analysis` into `Sprocket.Core.Stabilization` ->
  Core is the keystone with zero dependencies (ARCHITECTURE.md §2); `MotionTrack` (Core) must hold a
  list of `FrameMotion`, and `Sprocket.Analysis`'s `MotionEstimator` (which already depends on Core)
  produces them — so the shared value types belong in Core, with Analysis consuming them via a new
  `using Sprocket.Core.Stabilization;`.
- Stabilization is a hard-coded pipeline case (like `Transform`), not a registry SkSL effect ->
  it needs `ResolvedEffect.SourceTime` + `MediaRefId?` (frame context beyond what registry effects
  get) to look up the clip's motion track via `IMotionTrackProvider`. This mirrors the plan's phase-4
  design (`case EffectTypeIds.Stabilization` in `SkiaEffectPipeline`, not deferred to this phase).
- `MotionTrack` binary format is version 2 from the start (not 1) -> the plan's phase 1 spec
  mentioned an optional points section as "format v2, readers accept v1" for phase 6's track-point
  overlay; building the version-guard and points-section support now (even though nothing writes
  points yet) avoids a breaking format change later. Version 1 is still accepted by the reader
  (`hasPoints` flag defaults false, points array is `null`).
- Effect presets set only solve parameters, not analysis/workflow toggles
  (`detailedAnalysis`/`showTrackPoints`/`hideBanner`) -> matches the plan note "readouts... not
  params" and keeps presets from silently changing an unrelated cache-invalidating setting
  (`detailedAnalysis` changes the cache key per the plan).
- `StabilizationSolver` implemented the full phase-2 spec inline (adaptive smoothing via wide-window
  robust-median velocity heuristic, not L1-optimal paths) -> the plan explicitly defers L1-optimal
  paths to a follow-on and describes "Smooth Camera" as exactly this adaptive-window approach.
